svg.text: Two kinds of disruption, two different defences
Involuntary — nobody chose it
a node fails · a kernel panics
a container is OOMKilled
Nothing negotiates. Your defences:
more than one replica · probes
spreading across nodes
Voluntary — the platform chose it
a node is drained for maintenance
an upgrade · a rebalance
Planned actions can wait:
a PodDisruptionBudget says how much
of your app must stay up meanwhile
minAvailable: 2
3 replicas → disruptionsAllowed: 1 — a drain proceeds, one Pod at a time
2 replicas → disruptionsAllowed: 0 — the drain WAITS, the node goes unpatched
The fix is more replicas than the floor, not a lower floor.
Three replicas on ONE node
is not three replicas: it is one failure
away from an outage, and one drain
away from a full restart.
Either way, it ends in the same sequence
1. the Pod leaves the Service's endpoints — AND, at the same moment, shutdown begins. Neither is instant.
2. preStop runs (cover that race), then SIGTERM arrives.
3. after terminationGracePeriodSeconds, SIGKILL. An app that ignores SIGTERM spends the whole budget, every time.
